(1) STN-cortico-muscular connectivity is correlated with akinesia and (2) that STN-corticostriatal connectivity is modulated by levodopa.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of oscillatory coupling between the STN, M1 and muscle in PD.
the functional role of oscillatory coupling within the cortico-basal ganglia motor loop.
the modulation of oscillatory activity in the motor system by movement and medication in Parkinson's disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STN-cortico-muscular loop represents a functional unit, the integrity of which is crucially affected in PD.
both coherence measures are altered in PD and are correlated with motor impairment, but are modulated by movement and medication differently.
STN-corticocortical and corticomuscular coherence play a role in motor control, but are not the sole determinants of motor performance in PD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the STN plays an important role for the generation of movement-related cortical activity.
the STN plays a central role in the modulation of oscillatory coupling between cortical areas and muscles.
both STN-cortico-muscular beta band and cortico-motor beta band coherence are reduced in patients with PD and are related to the severity of the disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the modulation of oscillatory coherence by levodopa and movement is not consistent across frequency bands and brain areas.
the STN is not a simple relay of cortical activity to the spinal cord, but rather a node of an extended motor system, whose function is modulated by movement and medication.
